subject: memcg stats flushing (WAS "Re: [PATCH] fuse: disable default bdi strictlimiting")

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Yosry Ahmed noted that adding per-memcg thresholding for flush caused regressions in microbenchmarks due to parent iteration in deep hierarchies, but considered the impact acceptable given the trade-off between charging/uncharging and stat updates.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed expressed concerns that the rstat rate-limiting may be arbitrary and suggested removing it, also noting that the current implementation bounds stats updates by time rather than the number of updates.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed noted that the rstat rate-limiting is arbitrary, relying on a fixed two-second time interval rather than stats updates, and suggested removing it to allow callers to have a higher stats updates threshold based on their error tolerance.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed expressed concerns about introducing two separate update schemes, one for stats and another for other cases, which he believes would add unnecessary complexity. He suggested moving everything to a new 'better' scheme if possible or having a different scheme just for stats where the current tradeoff doesn't apply.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed expressed concerns that the cost of a normal flush could become high in cases with large trees, many CPUs, and/or high cgroup lock contention, potentially leading to hard lockups.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed expressed strong disagreement with the ratelimited flush mechanism, stating that it practically results in most cases not flushing at all and is an arbitrary way to feel good about skipping a flush.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed expressed concerns about the rate-limited flush for limit checking, citing potential performance issues and lock contention at high depths, and suggested removing the rate-limiting to allow callers to set a higher stats updates threshold.
sentiment_signals: considered a general indicator of acceptable performance
reviews.raw_body:
FWIW, when I added the per-memcg thresholding for flush (i.e.
stats_updates), there were some regressions in some microbenchmarks on
the update side due to the parent iteration in deep hierarchies.
However, we decided the regressions were acceptable because they were
of low significance compared to the extra of charging/uncharging in
those deep hierarchies. As you said, charges are not 1:1 to stat
updates, but it was considered a general indicator of acceptable
performance for the workload at that depth. That is all obviously very
hand wavy :)

---

Yeah it could be a problem, but I think we won't know for sure until
we run a reclaim-heavy workload (e.g. build the kernel in a constraint
cgroup) and check for actual regressions. I am often surprised by what
actually shows up (or doesn't) in higher-level workloads.

---

Yeah. I count 54 stats, with 8 bytes per counter that's ~7 cachelines
(on x86_64). I can see that being really expensive, but I can also see
it disappear into the noise if the stats updated together live in
close cachelines and the CPU prefetches surrounding cachelines.

---

Right. I am just trying to avoid the complexity of having two update
schemes if we can help it. If we can move everything to a new "better"
scheme, that would be great. But it might be the case that we have to
have a different scheme just for stats where the current update/read
tradeoff doesn't make sense.

---

I don't remember why ratelimiting was added, but I suspect for cases
with large trees, high number of CPUs, and/or high cgroup lock
contention -- the cost of a normal flush could get really high. Back
in the day when we used to always flush the entire tree (before
per-memcg thresholding), we ran into hard lockups for flushes taking

---

100% agreed. I never liked the ratelimited flush tbh. I think we
practically end up just not flushing in most cases (but I never really
checked), so it's just a way to feel good about skipping a flush :P

---

I would like to avoid the ratelimited flush for the limit checking for
the same reasons discussed above. I think we were all under the
assumption that the limit is rarely set in practice (other than 0 or
max), until we saw [*].

[*]https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260817131843.45121-1-husong@kylinos.cn/.

2026-08-28.patch_summary: This patch addresses the issue of high overhead in memcg stats flushing, particularly at high depths (8-16) where the extra latency can be up to 48ns. The problem arises from the use of rstat rate-limiting, which is arbitrary and bounded by time rather than actual stats updates. The proposed solution involves minimizing unnecessary overhead by not updating stats that don't require precision, and removing the rate-limiting mechanism. This approach aims to strike a balance between precision and performance, especially in scenarios where lock contention is a concern.
